criteria.evidence: All numeric claims in executive_summary and negotiation_analysis check out against the case data: $7,225 = $3,400 (E-1) + $3,825 (E-2) matching F-219; $11,920 = $10,070 (F-215) + $1,850 (F-216) matching F-217; the 8/9/5/14-unit breakdown is internally consistent at $425/unit across E-1, E-2 and E-3; the EDI-vs-POD, markdown-exclusion, and comparables figures (F-223-227) are stated exactly as given. No misstated value, direction or relationship was found.

The draft reply states the freight-refund ask is warranted 'given the shipment was in fact delivered several days past the requested date' — no fact in the case data (F-185, D-08, or any entitlement) establishes a specific delay magnitude ('several days'); only carrier-side causes (terminal backlog, driver-hours stand-down) are documented, not a days-late figure, so this is an invented specific asserted beyond the record.

The counter ($11,920.00), the conceded markdown ('We're not asking BlueLine to treat this as a covered loss'), the held disputed units/fees (5 damaged units, inspection fee, repack labor all pressed in the counter), and the goodwill framing of the freight charge ('goodwill gesture' / 'commercial accommodation') all match F-215–F-222 and entitlements E-3/E-6/E-7 exactly.

Recommendations are explicitly flagged ('Recommendation: given this exclusion, Northstar should concede the markdown outright...'; 'Recommendation: the comparables argue for pressing...'), factual claims carry bracketed citations throughout, and open items (D-04 EDI/POD, D-06 photo gap, G-02 packaging spec) are consistently described as unresolved rather than settled.

The brief addresses all five material items: the disputed 5 damaged units (para 2), the markdown exclusion (para 3), the EDI-vs-POD count conflict (exec summary + para 1 + a dedicated next step), the freight-refund goodwill angle (para 3), and the evidence gaps G-01–G-04 (each has a corresponding recommended_next_steps action).
